walkthroughs.body_html:
Photography — a core area of A-Level Art & Design.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Photography brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Photography.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Which photographer coined the phrase 'decisive moment'?
options: Robert Capa
Henri Cartier-Bresson
Don McCullin
Diane Arbus

mcqs.q: Which setting most directly controls depth of field?
options: ISO
Shutter speed
Aperture
White balance

mcqs.q: What is the significance of Duchamp's 'Fountain'?
options: It is a study of plumbing.
Researching the artist's life.
It challenged the definition of art - the artist's choice, not their skill, becomes the artwork.
It demonstrated his sculpting ability.

mcqs.q: What is the first step of formal analysis?
options: Researching the artist's life.
Patrons painted the works themselves.
Description - noting what is actually present in the work.
Interpretation - explaining what it means.

mcqs.q: Why is understanding patronage important for studying historical art?
options: Patrons painted the works themselves.
Patrons commissioned art for specific purposes, shaping content and form.
Artists worked freely - patronage was irrelevant to the artwork.
It is a study of plumbing.
